text:
alicia: Heads up — I got a report from support that when users rapidly switch workspaces the top-left workspace banner briefly shows the wrong org name. Saw it locally too. Screenshot: https://img.internal/repro/1954321098.png

sam: repro steps? can try to bisect the frontend bundle.

alicia: 1) login as alice@acme, 2) open console, 3) click workspace dropdown and switch to engineering, 4) quickly hit back to acme org. The banner flashes the *previous* org for ~200-400ms. Happens more on slow networks.

ben: this sounds like client-side cache + optimistic UI. Are we trusting a cached workspace name instead of the authoritative /api/workspace/:id metadata?

alicia: yeah looks like that. We only fetch the full workspace object when the route change completes, but we render using last-selected name from localStorage first.

iqra: any telemetry showing cross-tenant reads or just UI label mismatch? need to know if data is leaking or just a visual glitch.

alicia: initial triage — so far only visual. No queries to other workspace resources in the network tab during the flash. But users reported seeing widgets update to the wrong workspace briefly too (charts).

ben: if charts are re-rendering with wrong context, that's more serious. Can you attach a HAR?

alicia: attached HAR and a small screen recording in the ticket. HAR shows a single call to /api/workspaces/current -> returns id X, then a delayed call to /api/workspaces/:id -> returns Y. In between, client uses local cache which still maps X->name of previous workspace.

sam: code snippet from frontend handler: ```js
setWorkspaceName(localCache[nameId] || optimisticName);
fetch(`/api/workspaces/${id}`).then(res => res.json()).then(w => setWorkspaceName(w.name));
```

sam: we rely on optimisticName to avoid flicker, but if the optimisticName map is keyed by an ephemeral session key we can easily show the wrong name during back-to-back switches.

ben: backend side: /api/workspaces/current is a proxy that tries to return the "active" workspace id quickly. Could be returning a stale value under heavy load if route resolution is racing with ACL refresh — but HAR shows it returned X then later /api/workspaces/:id returned Y, so the sequence is correct. Seems client is rendering stale mapping for id -> name.

iqra: from SRE perspective, this is a UI scoping bug unless we see cross-tenant resource access. But UX-wise it's still a high-severity bug because customers could misinterpret context when acting.

alicia: agree. Proposed fixes: 1) clear optimistic local cache on any workspace switch event, 2) make the client render a skeleton until authoritative /api/workspaces/:id returns if switch happened within last 500ms, 3) add a safety header on internal API responses that includes workspace id AND a request-scoped nonce so the client can detect mismatches. Thoughts?

sam: (1) low-risk hotfix we can ship today. (2) might increase perceived latency — but better than incorrect context. Maybe do a quick experiment toggling skeleton only for app routes that affect data (dashboards/forms) not the whole console.

ben: (3) header is interesting. We already have X-Workspace-Id header on responses for routing, we could add X-Workspace-Nonce that the server rotates on context change. Client can assert that the header matches the expected id before applying cached derived state.

alicia: perfect. Also adding a client-side telemetry counter for "workspace-id-mismatch-on-render" with tags: prev_id, new_id, route, user_id, network_rtt_bucket. That will help measure how often visual mismatch correlates with data re-render.

iqra: please make sure telemetry doesn't include PII. Use hashed user bucket. SRE can set alert if mismatch rate > 0.5% of switches in prod.

sam: planning: push quick cache-clear hotfix to canary in next hour, then monitor telemetry. If it drops to 0 -> backport to stable. If charts still show wrong data, we escalate to server-side enforcement.

ben: low-level internal API debate — do we rely on clients to enforce workspace scoping for UI labels, or should server responses include canonical display names to avoid round trips? If we send canonical display name in every response that's extra bytes but it removes a class of bugs.

alicia: prefer server-provided canonical fields for critical UI bits (display name, short id). Non-critical stuff can remain cached. Balance bandwidth vs safety.

sam: deploy-bot: canary deploy started by sam for frontend @ 1954321280 :rocket:

deploy-bot: canary healthy at 60% traffic.

alicia: monitoring now. adding unit test for cache-clear on workspace-switch and an integration test that simulates rapid toggles.

iqra: create an incident stub? may not need full page but let's create a P1 if we see mismatches affecting data. For now log as SEV-2.

ben: filed PR for server header change, link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pulls/3128

sam: PR for frontend hotfix in review: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pulls/3130

alicia: thanks. will follow up with a short doc in #eng-platform about which UI fields must be canonical from server vs allowed to be optimistic.

iqra: thumbs up. keep me posted. :eyes:
